summary: Standing steel fire tower in O'Bannon Woods State Park, Indiana; NHLR dates the first CCC fire tower on the site to 1937 and a fire-damage rebuild, a steel tower, to 1941.

facts.design: 88-ft steel tower with 7'x7' metal cab (NHLR); hobbyist survey gives 100 ft for the earlier CCC steel tower

visit.trail_note: Hobbyist site reports the cab can be climbed into; confirm with O'Bannon Woods State Park before visiting.

events.note: Annual report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts: temporary wooden tower built at the Harrison County State Forest near Wyandotte Cave. Link to this exact site not confirmed.
Sign reads 'Erected: 1932' (hobbyist site). The survey notes dispute which tower the sign refers to.
February 1932 newspaper: 2,600 acres acquired; a 60-ft temporary wooden tower planned, to be replaced with steel later.
NHLR: CCC constructed the tower in 1937. Hobbyist survey: a 100-ft CCC steel tower replaced the wooden tower by 1937.
NHLR: tower damaged by fire and replaced with 88-ft steel tower with 7x7 metal cab. Sign reads 'Rebuilt 1941'. Year of the fire not given.

evidence.supports: tower is in O'Bannon Woods State Park, formerly part of Harrison-Crawford State Forest
evidence.quote: Location: O’Bannon Woods State Park (previously part of Harrison-Crawford State Forest)
County: Harrison (the only tower in this county)

evidence.supports: first tower was temporary wooden, 55 ft (survey)
evidence.quote: the first tower, intended as temporary, was a fifty-five (55) foot wooden pole tower

evidence.supports: 1928 annual report mention of temporary wooden tower near Wyandotte Cave
evidence.quote: A temporary wooden tower has been built at the Harrison County State Forest near Wyandotte Cave.
Two thousand six hundred acres of woodland in Scott and Spencer townships, Harrison county, were acquired this week by the state in its reforestation program.

evidence.supports: 1932 planned 60-ft temporary wood tower to be replaced by steel
evidence.quote: A temporary wood tower, sixty feet high and twelve feet square at the base, soon will be erected. It will be replaced later by one of steel.

evidence.supports: CCC constructed the first tower in 1937
evidence.quote: The first fire tower on this site on the Harrison Crawford State Forest was constructed by the CCC in 1937.

evidence.supports: fire damage, 1941 replacement with 88-ft steel tower and 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: It was damaged by fire and replaced with the 88’ steel tower with 7’x7’ metal cab in 1941.
“Erected: 1932; Burned; Rebuilt 1941” — according to the sign at the tower.

evidence.supports: 100-ft CCC steel tower replaced wooden tower by 1937
evidence.quote: It was replaced by a one hundred (100) foot steel tower (erected by Civilian Conservation Corps) by 1937.

evidence.supports: land transferred to O'Bannon Woods State Park; tower renamed
evidence.quote: When the land was transferred to the O’Bannon Woods State Park, the tower became known as the O'Bannon Woods Fire Tower.
Condition: Standing; climbable up into cab. Great climb, great view.

evidence.supports: 1928 date of the annual report quoted by Forest Lookouts
evidence.quote: Annual Report - Indiana Department of Conservation - 1928

evidence.supports: February 1932 date of the Indianapolis News report

corrections.proposed: 1937 built by CCC; 1941 rebuilt after fire damage
corrections.why: NHLR description dates the first CCC tower to 1937 and says the 1941 steel tower replaced one damaged by fire; its Built field alone is incomplete.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1937 (CCC) then fire damage and a 1941 rebuild. The sign reads Erected 1932, Burned, Rebuilt 1941, and the hobbyist survey places a CCC steel tower by 1937. The story reports the NHLR sequence and notes the sign and survey versions.
NHLR gives 88 ft for the 1941 steel tower; the hobbyist survey gives 100 ft for the earlier CCC steel tower. height_m uses the NHLR figure for the standing tower.
The 1932 newspaper says 60 ft; the hobbyist survey says 55 ft.

notes_for_editor: Construction sequence before 1941 is disputed between the NHLR (CCC 1937, fire, 1941 rebuild) and the sign and hobbyist survey (1932 erected). Staffing, fire year and official access status were not found in the pages read. Climbability rests on one hobbyist site and needs confirmation with the state park. Living New Deal page returned 403; Wikipedia O'Bannon Woods page had no tower text in the fetched output. Agency left out because the NHLR administered-by value did not appear in the fetched text.
